outcome: obstetrical interventions (caesarean sections, episiotomies, forceps deliveries)
cohort: The study participants were mothers and infants recorded in archival datasets from Basel and Lausanne, Switzerland, during the 1920s.
finding: Key findings indicated that larger foetal head diameters and narrower pelvic measurements were linked to prolonged expulsion phases and an increased likelihood of obstetric intervention.
mod_finding: Larger foetal head diameters, narrower pelvic measurements, abnormal head positions, first-time births, and maternal rickets were associated with an increased likelihood of episiotomies, forceps deliveries, and caesarean sections.
